method_p1: event-driven counterfactual bridge: w bridges event u->v if history has u->w incoming and w->v outgoing; signal per bridge = 1/outdeg(w), I_cf(w) = sum of its share of each bridged event's total 2-hop signal
interpretation: P1 and P3 are complementary signals: top-1% sets overlap in only 14 of 144 wallets.
P1 at 1% captures 47.9% of all information-bridge events (vs 29.2% P3, 36.7% raw volume, 5.5% random); at 10% 91.2%, at 20% 97.9%.
P3 remains best on raw hard-event coverage (22.7% at 1%) because it is defined on event consequence; P1 is best on the information-flow signal it is defined on.
quota_half_P1_half_P3 gives a balanced allocation (40.5% bridge + 19.2% hard-event coverage at 1%), motivating the learned P4 router to mix both features per budget.
boundaries: P1 here is a graph-information occlusion proxy (2-hop path availability), not an LLM/GNN leave-one-wallet-out retraining experiment; the latter is the stronger v2 (train cheap sequence model, mask rows, re-score neighbours).
Bridge existence uses only pre-Aug history; test event identities are used only to measure coverage (selection-layer evaluation). Production router training must use May/Jun snapshots.
internal_trace (auxiliary) excluded; directional role semantics follow target_event_sequences_v1.
